title: Virtual Reality Confrontation with the Inner Critic
summary:
Depressive patients are often affected by strong, self-deprecating thoughts that contribute to the development and solidification of their depression. In Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), patients learn to build up a mental distance to such thoughts with the help of so-called defusion techniques. Schema therapy works on self-deprecating thoughts by asking patients to imagine their inner critic as a person sitting opposite them in a chair dialogue and making the same accusations. However, this method requires patients to be able and motivated to visualise their inner critic. This is a challenge for some groups of people. As depression is often accompanied by a lack of motivation and a decline in cognitive performance, this is a particularly difficult task for depressed people. With virtual reality, we want to give patients the opportunity to confront their inner critic in an immersive way. To this end, two personalised avatars of themselves will be created for each participant in the experimental condition, one of which will represent their inner critic and the other a supportive component of themselves. In the session, they will then encounter accusations from the inner critic referring to a personal self-deprecating thought and counteract them with defusion techniques from ACT.
In this first study we target the feasibility of our study concept including two methods of ACT.

interventions.name: Confrontation of the personal inner critic, represented by an individualized self-avatar in a virtual reality environment and utilization of methods for cognitive defusion (method A via exposure and method B via introduction of a contextual cue) to cope with self-devaluating thoughts-Methodorder A&B

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosed (recurrent) depressive episode
Sufficent understanding of German language
Current medication, psychotherapy or other S3-guideline compliant treatment for depressive disorders
Normal (or corrected) vision capacity
Exclusion criteria:
Psychotic symptoms, demential symptoms, schizophrenia, epilepsy, bipolar depression, addiction disorders, severe neurological disorders, signs of severe risk for suicide
